root.name: Italian Game: Hungarian Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7

overview: Black declines to mirror White with ...Bc5 and keeps the bishop home on e7, accepting a slightly cramped position for safety. White usually plays 4.d4 and takes the centre; Black either exchanges on d4 or holds with ...d6 and develops with ...Nf6 and ...O-O. The game is steady, with White holding a modest space edge and Black waiting to break with ...d5 or ...exd4.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4 and c3, keeping the bishop on c4 eyeing f7.
Use the extra space to develop quickly and castle before Black frees the position.

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...exd4 and ...d5, or hit back with the Tartakower ...Ne4 after 6.e5.

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on c3, d4 and e4 against Black's compact ...d6/...e5 centre.
Open game after ...exd4 Nxd4 with symmetrical development.

character.notes: Passive, safe Black set-up; White has no forcing attack. Few ways for either side to lose quickly.

soundness.notes: Sound; White keeps a small edge.

structure.notes: Main line 4.d4 exd4 5.c3 or 5.Nxd4 opens the centre; with ...d6 it stays in tension.

approach.notes: Recognised sideline, played now and then by strong players as a safe reply; not a system.

level.notes: Few forced lines; moderate understanding of when to break the centre.

sublines_that_differ.name: Tartakower Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7 4. d4 exd4 5. c3 Nf6 6. e5 Ne4
sublines_that_differ.how: More tactical, Black's knight sits on e4 and White gambits a pawn on d4 for activity.

character.reason: Passive but hard-to-break Black set-up with no forcing play.

gambit.reason: No material offered in the main line.

soundness.reason: A sound if slightly worse reply for Black.

structure.reason: 4.d4 exd4 leads to an open Scotch-like game.

approach.reason: A recognised sideline, not a system and not seldom-used enough for offbeat.

plans.reason: White's d4 centre against Black's cramped set-up.
